summary: Remote-controlled daemon accepts shell/PTY commands from WebSocket gateway
details: @whalent/agent installs a daemon (`whalent`, entry dist/index.cjs) that connects outbound to a WebSocket gateway (wss://) and, per the shipped README, accepts remote commands including `upgrade` and `restart` from that gateway. The bundled runtime pulls in `ws`, `node-pty`, `ssh2`, and `@xterm/headless`, and the code references child_process spawning and local RDP (127.0.0.1:3389) / VNC (127.0.0.1:5900/5901) endpoints, giving the gateway operator the ability to drive an interactive shell/PTY, self-upgrade the client, and reach local remote-desktop services on the host running the daemon. Both distributed files (dist/index.cjs and the 13.9 MB dist/core.cjs) are heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (string-array + RC4/base64 decoder, hex-mangled `_0xNNNN` identifiers, control-flow flattening); the build script that produced them is not shipped, so the exact set of commands the gateway can issue to the client cannot be read from the tarball. Whoever controls the gateway URL (the default endpoint or a `--gateway` override pointed at an attacker-controlled server) has interactive code-execution and remote-desktop-adjacent access on the host running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
